title: KV compression sensitivity probe: FP8/INT8/INT4 memory vs quality trade-offs
creator: Ayesha Patel
description:
Objective: run a focused, reproducible set of experiments to measure the memory savings, latency impact, and generation-quality trade-offs when applying different KV cache compression/quantization schemes (FP8, INT8, INT4) to large decoder-only models under continuous-batching workloads. We aim to produce a recommendation matrix that maps workload characteristics (seq len, batch size, kv hit rate) to the preferred KV storage format and fallback policies for Redwood runtime.

Background: continuous batching and aggressive KV caching are key levers for cost and throughput. However, KV cache can dominate GPU memory at long context lengths or when many concurrent requests are pinned. Quantizing the cached keys/values could substantially reduce memory pressure but may introduce subtle generation quality regressions or instability under certain sequence lengths. Prior artifacts: ENG-7532 and ENG-9821 performed benchmarks and mixed-precision probes; this ticket focuses specifically on systematic sensitivity analysis across FP8/INT8/INT4 formats and adaptive hybrid strategies (e.g., high-precision head/tail, lossy compression for older prefixes).
acceptance_criteria: Run deterministic eval suite across 3 model sizes (7B, 13B, 70B) with baseline (FP16) and quantized KV formats (FP8, INT8, INT4)

Produce per-format metrics: memory footprint delta, p95 latency under continuous-batching, end-to-end RTF for interactive workload, and quality deltas (BLEU/Rouge where applicable, and human-rated pass/fail on 250 prompt set)
Identify at least two safe heuristics for runtime selection (e.g., quantize only tail KV beyond N tokens; use INT8 for 7B with seq<=4k; fallback to FP16 when perplexity regression > X%)
Publish experiment notebook, raw traces, and a short PRD with recommended runtime changes for a canary rollout
methodology: Quantization implementations will use the runtime's kernel-friendly layouts; compare symmetric/asymmetric int quantization and FP8 variants aligned with model weight formats

Evaluation datasets: 1) WikiLong (synthetic long-context continuations), 2) Redwood internal prompt set (250 prompts across instruction/chat/dialogue use-cases), 3) adversarial continuity set (context-injection tests)
Workloads: continuous-batching driver that simulates 100 concurrent connections with variable arrival rates and pinned KV keys; test seq lens: 1k, 4k, 16k where supported

Metrics: GPU memory used for KV cache only (MB), total GPU memory, latency p50/p95, throughput (tokens/s), generation-quality delta vs FP16 baseline using automated metrics and a small blinded human eval
plan: Week 0: implement INT8/INT4 packing and FP8 conversion paths in a branch (ENG-11427-kv-quant) — code skeleton and CI smoke tests
Week 1: microbenchmarks for kernel correctness and perf (single-stream regeneration, KV read/write integrity tests)
Week 2: run distributed continuous-batching scenarios across three instance types (A100-40GB, A100-80GB, H100-80GB); collect traces and memory profiles
Week 3: quality evaluation + human annotation, collate results and draft PRD with runtime heuristics
Canary: prepare a canary runtime flag gated behind a feature flag for 5% of traffic if results justify rollout
updates: 2025-02-21: Branch created (github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/compare/ENG-11427-kv-quant). Basic FP8 conversion implemented; unit tests added for numeric invertibility on small tensors. — Marco Ruiz

2025-02-24: Microbenchmarks: INT8 packing reduced KV memory by ~2.9x vs FP16 on 7B; INT4 shows 5.6x but observed small artifacts on beam-search for long-range coref examples. Preliminary notes attached to doc.

2025-02-26: Observed a p95 latency increase of ~6-8% for INT4 on A100-40GB due to extra unpacking ops; FP8 has near-zero latency delta. Spike analyzed with nvprof traces (links in artifacts). — profiling team

2025-03-01: Ran first human eval (100 prompts): INT8 pass rate 96% vs FP16 baseline 98%; INT4 pass rate 88% with concentrated failures on factuality in multi-turn dialogue. Decided to test hybrid strategy: keep head KV in FP16 for last N=512 tokens. — Design & Research feedback

2025-03-03: Implemented hybrid heuristic (head FP16 + tail INT8) and re-ran reproducibility suite; memory savings remain ~2.4x for 13B with negligible quality delta. Draft PRD updated with recommendation.
decisions: Do not recommend blanket INT4 for production at this time due to observed quality regressions in multi-turn dialogue and latency overhead for unpacking on older kernels.
Adopt INT8 as default candidate for smaller models (<=13B) under high memory pressure, with automatic fallback to FP16 when human-quality delta threshold exceeded.
Use FP8 as a low-risk option on H100 hardware where kernels are optimized; still require cross-checking for model-specific sensitivity
Add runtime flag 'kv.quant.strategy' with values [off, int8, int4, fp8, hybrid-head-fp16-tail-int8] to enable canary experiments
risks: Quality regressions for multi-turn dialogues with coreference — medium risk if INT4 used indiscriminately
Kernel unpack overhead increases tail latency for some instance types — could violate SLA p95
Quantized representations may interact poorly with other runtime optimizations (prefix-caching, KV dedupe) requiring additional integration testing
Human evaluation scale is small; larger-scale A/B needed before production rollout
metrics: KV memory reduction (MB) and ratio vs FP16
Automated quality deltas (BLEU/Rouge/spBLEU where relevant) and human pass-rate delta
Canary error rate and rollback triggers (e.g., >1.5x baseline error or >3% human-quality drop)
next_steps: Complete expanded human-eval (additional 150 prompts focusing on multi-turn factuality)
Instrument canary flags and monitoring alerts in Console dashboards
Plan an A/B trial on dedicated capacity with two customer sandboxes to validate user-visible regressions
If A/B is successful, schedule a runtime release with controlled rollout in runtime-1.21
